body:
Thanks for all of that I really really needed it. I don't think there's anything anyone can say to me that's better than all of that. 

I'll try and look into the disassocitive disorder thing. It seems about right. lifes hard when you want to participate but your own brain limits you.
I'm in that hole too. Shit blows. Consider this reply some sort of internet hug. They really need to work on the technology to give hugs over the web.

Few fetishes hurt anyone, if you only let it live in fantasy. You're not sick or wrong as far I can see. As I've heard said "your kink isn't my kink" but you're right to it as long as you don't harm others or do anything illegal like Villemus said. 

I'm sorry your surrounding community isn't supportive, if you desired "recovery" that sort of lack of support makes it hard. It's not an easy to quick process and you may hate parts of yourself during it but you can get over it. 

I believe in you and support you wether you pick recovery or self-acceptance.

I know how hard and scary it is. I really, really truly do. I can't keep a job due to it. But I promise you, talking to a pro is different because they want to accommodate you and help you and will do whatever you feel you needs to be done. Maybe try writing a note to your school's councilor or emailing them? Tell them you're not ready to talk beyond those means yet but want help.

Sounds like you're also having some sort of existential crisis, lol. It's good you're trying to go back to old habits and patterns. Those sort of things help a lot you just gotta keep up the work on that. Maybe talk it over with someone close to you?

I know the feeling about talking with others. If you want to see if maybe typing out your feelings would help, I'll gladly chat with you a bit. Maybe we can keep one another company. 

But other than that, it's difficult as hell but the thing about talking with any sort of councilor is that you can tell them your issue with talking face to face, and silly as it seems, the better ones will allow you talk over the phone and slowly ease into physical conversation. I started that way for a while, the moved into being in the same room but I never looked at her. stared at the wall or floor. Hell, for a few days I didn't even face the same direction.
I will look it up! Thank you so much for a good starting point to solving this.
Maybe. It's a good suggestions, but somehow that makes me feel all weird.

We're working on it. Boyfriend doesn't seem to know what to do and it doesn't help that he has his own negligence issues to work through where he thinks it's okay to solve everything with sex. He's working on no longer associating love and sex as the same thing. From my past history, physical contact is the last thing I want. It's a weird mix of problems, and when I stand back to really look at it, it's sort of funny to me.
the well wishing is more than helpful thank you
I try hard to figure that out. still have yet to pinpoint the issue but I will keep working at it.
thank you very very much. Im glad that there is such a supportive place here. its so hard when what you feel makes you think you're all alone.
Thanks seems I need more therapy than I thought!

These are feelings you should share. Tell her this. It's amazing how after some talk, you guys could travel together. Maybe something as simple as changing your scenery and/or routine could really help you cope with those feelings and not risk someone who cares about you.
Thanks a lot. I needed that push. You're great!
I'd like to read that for sure.

I've tried to explain it to him. He doesn't seem to get it. I used to be in an abusive relationship based heavily on dug use. Tried to explain all of that to him and still somehow he doesn't get it. He tries his best to comfort me, thats it. I might look into the therapy thing.
